tasks.old_behavior: GUserDirectory enum has members DESKTOP through VIDEOS (8 members). G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES sentinel equals 8. Any code iterating i=0..G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES-1 processes 8 directories.
tasks.new_behavior: GUserDirectory enum gains G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS after VIDEOS. G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES sentinel now equals 9. Code iterating i=0..G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES-1 processes 9 directories, including the new PROJECTS slot. Code that statically initializes arrays of size G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES will have one extra element.
tasks.compatibility_reason: Adding a new enum value at the end of GUserDirectory changes the integer value of G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES from 8 to 9. This is an ABI change: any existing compiled code that uses G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES as an array bound or loop sentinel will have a mismatched size when linked against the new library. C code compiled with the old header that uses switch() without default will not handle the new value. The enum documentation explicitly states 'The #GUserDirectory enumeration can be extended at later date', so this is an expected additive change, but still a binary-incompatible sentinel shift for any code compiled against the old header and linked against the new library.
tasks.test_recommendation: Write a regression test that iterates all GUserDirectory values from 0 to G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES-1 and calls g_get_user_special_dir() for each, verifying that the new PROJECTS slot returns a valid path (or NULL if not configured). Verify that g_icon_name lookups for the PROJECTS path return the expected icon. Recompile existing test suites against the new header to catch any array-size mismatch.

tasks.old_behavior: When the path matches G_USER_DIRECTORY_PICTURES but not any earlier directory check, the if-else chain falls through to the else clause returning NULL. The projects directory path (if PROJECTS were resolvable by some other means) would result in no icon name match.
tasks.new_behavior: When the path matches g_get_user_special_dir(G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS), the new else-if branch returns 'folder-projects-symbolic' or 'folder-projects' as the icon name instead of falling through to NULL. The observable effect is that g_file_query_info() on a path matching the projects directory now returns an icon instead of no icon.
tasks.compatibility_reason: This is an additive behavioral change: a new code path is added for the new G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS enum value. Existing compiled code can only reach this new code path if it is recompiled with the new header (to access G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS) or if it iterates over all G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES values. The change is triggered by the new enum value being used as an argument to g_get_user_special_dir(). Since the icon is returned via g_file_info_set_icon() / g_file_info_set_symbolic_icon(), any application that queries file info and displays icons may now show a different icon for the projects directory.
tasks.test_recommendation: Write a test that sets XDG_PROJECTS_DIR to a temporary directory, calls g_file_query_info() on that directory, and verifies that the returned icon name contains 'folder-projects'. Also verify that the icon is non-NULL and has a non-empty name.
